subject: ela
skillName: Compare fictional portrayals to historical accounts
intro: Compare historical fiction to historical accounts.

items.prompt:
Historical fiction usually KEEPS from history the:
A) real setting and events
B) nothing
C) only the title

Historical fiction INVENTS the:
A) characters and dialogue
B) real dates
C) real battles

A history textbook mainly gives:
A) facts
B) invented dialogue
C) imaginary heroes

A novel set in a real war invents a soldier and his letters but keeps the real battles and dates. What is INVENTED?
A) the battles
B) the soldier and his letters
C) the dates
items.answer: B) the soldier and his letters

steps: Character and letters are fiction. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) the soldier and his letters

items.prompt:
Why might an author invent a character for a real historical event?
A) to make history feel personal and emotional
B) to hide the facts
C) to make it boring
items.answer: A) to make history feel personal and emotional

steps: Fiction personalizes history. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) to make history feel personal and emotional

items.prompt:
Compared to a historical account, a historical NOVEL adds:
A) imagined characters, dialogue, and emotions
B) only dates
C) nothing
items.answer: A) imagined characters, dialogue, and emotions

steps: Fiction adds story. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) imagined characters, dialogue, and emotions

items.prompt:
A novelist changes the date of a real battle to fit her plot. Comparing the novel to a history book, a reader should understand that:
A) the novel altered a fact for storytelling
B) the history book is wrong
C) both are pure fiction
items.answer: A) the novel altered a fact for storytelling

steps: Fiction can alter history. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) the novel altered a fact for storytelling

items.prompt:
Reading BOTH a historical novel and a factual account of the same era helps a reader:
A) tell what is real history from what the author imagined
B) ignore history
C) assume the novel is all true
items.answer: A) tell what is real history from what the author imagined

steps: Compare to separate fact and fiction. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) tell what is real history from what the author imagined
